T.D. Lewis Re-elected Montreal YMCA President. 
Three French Community Leaders Named Directors.

POUR RENSEIGNEMENTS 
COMMUNIQUER AVEC W. Sher 
|CONTACT 


T. Denton Lewis, General Manager, Securities, Bank of 
Montreal, was re-elected yesterday as President of the YMCA of 
Montreal. 
Also voted in for another term as officers were: 
H. Roy Crabtree, Honorary President; W.N. Hall, Lettres zatdents 
W.S. Kirkpatrick, 2nd Vice-president; J.D. Houlding, 3rd Vice-president; 
W.C. Corbett, Honorary Treasurer. 
Three prominent French community leaders joined Louis Hébert, 
President of Banque Canadienne Nationale, on the Montreal Y's board of 
directors. 
They are: Pierre Delagrave, Vice-president, Public and 
Employee Relations, Domtar Limited; Claude Hébert, President, 
Transparent Paper Products; Claude Robillard, President, Fraser-Brace 
Engineering Co. Ltd. 
ris 
7 SFD Dupe Continued 
Ie Wb 


«Pen 

Other newcomers to the board are David Gill, Vice-president 
of Nesbitt Thomson and Company Limited and Robert H. Hoppe, President 
of Stuart Brothers Limited. 

The five men, all elected for initial three-year terms, will 
help formulate policies governing all YMCA activities in the Greater 
Montreal area. 

As a Quebec organization, the Montreal YMCA is eager to 
participate in the province's evolution, particularly in the field 
of education, where it feels it can make a significant contribution. 

The Y rejects the narrow concept that the main objective of 
education is to help prepare a person to earn a living. It should be 
a never-ending process of growth, directed towards individual self- 


fulfillment. 


Continued 


"The educational revolution taking place in the province is 
based on principles and insights very much akin to those which are 
valued by the YMCA,'"' states R.G. Rogers, assistant general secretary 


of the Association. 


"Tt is our job to let ourselves be known, to interpret what 


and who we are, and what we are trying to do," he adds.
